_meta.note: All stock/price figures below are LIVE parts_search.py re-verifications run 2026-08-07 during P3, not carried from P1/P2 research without re-check. See OPEN in the handoff message for the one build-blocking finding (EPC2019 out of stock).

parts.role: 40V DC bus input, >=6A. CONFIRMED THT (only THT part on the board, by architecture design - blocks.md/sheets.md already place it at x<5mm, outside the [5,10,36,70] heatsink land, HS-3). This is a pre-resolved exception to single-sided SMT assembly, not a new conflict: JLC PCBA supports a single THT part mixed with SMT on an otherwise top-side-only build. No action needed, just confirming the placement discipline stays intact at P6.

alternates.note: RECOMMENDED FREE UPGRADE, needs an owner ruling. 100uF 80V, identical D10xL10.5mm can and therefore the identical footprint, stock 61436 (2.6x deeper), $0.1703 (marginally CHEAPER). Only difference is the voltage rating: it takes the ~51V LC inrush overshoot from 81% of rating down to 64%, which is the difference between 'inside the usual 80% electrolytic derating guideline' and 'comfortably inside it'. Not swapped in unilaterally because 63V is the architecture's documented spec and the handoff named C51953411 explicitly - see OPEN.

parts.role: Bulk on +40V at the terminal. RE-SOURCED 2026-08-07: the previous entry C54321630 / MA63V100M10X10 has NO EasyEDA CAD data (3 pull attempts failed, not a 403/rate-limit pattern), so it could never reach a footprint. Swapped to the documented alternate, which pulls cleanly (footprint CAP-SMD_BD10.0-L10.3-W10.3-LS11.0-FD_1, symbol registered) and is deeply stocked - 23372 vs the 5x10=50 required, 467x margin. Still an SMD can with no bottom-face leads, so the heatsink face stays clear. 63V rating still satisfies the P1 finding that LC inrush overshoots to ~51V (transient 81% of rating; steady-state 40V = 63%). DIELECTRIC SUBSTITUTED POLYMER -> ALUMINIUM ELECTROLYTIC: the old entry was specified as a polymer cap, and this replacement is a plain aluminium electrolytic with much higher ESR (order 0.4-1 ohm vs order 20 mohm) and a modest 200mA@120Hz ripple rating. Judged acceptable, and flagged rather than hidden, because this cap is DC-bus hold-up only, not an RF part: at 20 MHz it is far past self-resonance and contributes nothing either way, and the switching-frequency and RF ripple are carried by C103/C104 (2.2uF 100V X7R) and the C207-C212 HF bank. If P4 finds the bus needs real low-ESR bulk, that is a re-source, not a tweak. FOOTPRINT NOTE: the pull shipped this part with attr 'through_hole' despite both lands being surface pads - corrected to 'smd' in the footprint, otherwise C101/C102 would have landed in the THT column of the P9 CPL and broken the single-sided-SMT build. A courtyard was also added; the pull shipped none.

Mid-frequency tier on +40V bus. PACKAGE SUBSTITUTED 0805->1206: the only 0805 2.2uF/100V X7R found at LCSC (CIA0805X7R225K101MT, C51295056) has stock=17, far short of the 5x-qty rule. 1206 is the same electrical part, just larger footprint - not load-bearing since this cap lives in zone A (plenty of room), not the tight switch cluster. X7R is correct here per architecture (bus tier, not tank).

alternates.note: Shenzhen Kinghelm, 50 ohm DC-6GHz, VSWR 1.35, stock 647, $0.5416 - 5.5x cheaper. Its pulled footprint is likewise F.Cu-only (4x 1.4mm square lands at 5.08mm pitch + 1.6mm centre land) and its datasheet's recommended PCB layout is 4 square lands + a centre circle, which is consistent with surface mount. NOT DATASHEET-CONFIRMED: the drawing's cross-section is ambiguous about whether the 4 SQ0.9 legs protrude below the seating plane, and the sheet lists a wave-solder rating. Do NOT substitute this in without re-reading the mechanical drawing to the same standard applied to the primary - that shortcut is exactly what produced the C496550 error.

parts.role: J201 = drive input (I1). J301 = RF output (I2), same part per architecture. RE-SOURCED 2026-08-07, replacing C496550 / BWSMA-KE-P001. MOUNT STYLE VERIFIED AGAINST THE MANUFACTURER DRAWING: TE customer drawing C-CONSMA001-SMD Rev G, SHEET 1, states verbatim 'Connector: SMA Jack (Female Socket)' and 'Termination: PCB Surface Mount'; SHEET 2 'RECOMMENDED FOOTPRINT' gives five top-side lands only (four 2.44mm squares at +/-2.66mm, one 2.05mm round centre, 7.76mm overall) with no drilled holes and no bottom-side copper, and sheet 1 DETAIL A specifies a 0.00-0.10mm centre-contact-to-mounting-plane standoff, i.e. nothing protrudes below the board. Local copy of that drawing is committed at parts/C22418168_TE_customer_drawing.pdf; the pulled EasyEDA footprint matches all three of its land dimensions exactly. WHY THE OLD PART WAS WRONG: C496550's LCSC listing says 'Board Side Inner hole Offset Pin SMA SMD' and its EasyEDA footprint is nominally 'SMD', but its manufacturer datasheet (parts/C496550.pdf pp.4-6) is a vertical THROUGH-HOLE 1/4-36 UNEF screw-thread panel-mount jack with 4 round pin legs, and its pulled footprint carries B.Cu lands. LCSC's package field and 'Board Side' connector type are NOT evidence of mount style in this category - the same wording appears on both parts. FLAT-HEATSINK IMPACT: none. Every land is F.Cu/F.Paste/F.Mask only, so unlike J101 these two connectors carry NO placement restriction relative to the [5,10,36,70] heatsink land, and the 100%-SMT goal is preserved. ELECTRICAL: 50 ohm, 18 GHz (LCSC) / 12.4 GHz (Linx) vs 20 MHz operation, and 100 Vrms / 141 Vpk / 2 Arms at 200 W into 50 ohm vs the ~335 Vrms standard SMA working class - electrically undemanding, as briefed, so mount style and stock drove the choice. STOCK/COST: 1744 in stock vs the 5x10=50 required (35x margin). Price is the one real regression: $2.97 vs $0.388, i.e. $29.74 vs $3.88 across the 10 pieces a 5-board build needs. That ~$26 delta buys the only SMA on the catalogue whose surface-mount termination is stated in the manufacturer's own drawing; see the alternate for a $0.54 option that would need the same verification done first.
50 ohm input termination (2x100R parallel). 125mW rating per part comfortably covers the ~0.0625W each sees. DC-coupled per architecture ruling D8 - no series cap.

parts.role: SINGLE-SOURCE IC, AUTHENTICITY RISK: this LCSC listing (C6423790) brands the part 'Tokmas', not Texas Instruments, despite carrying TI's exact MPN. Carried forward from P0/P1 as an explicit flag (OPEN-6 in decisions.md) - verify authenticity on receipt, or use the genuine-TI alternate C506817 instead. No other pin-compatible low-side GaN driver at this speed class exists at LCSC (see board LEARNINGS.md: LMG1210/LMG1205/UCC27714/IR2304/IR21844/FAN73932/SLM2101 were all already surveyed and rejected at P0/P1 for wrong topology or 100s-of-kHz speed class).
LMG1020 VDD bypass, primary. Per architecture: <0.5mm from the VDD ball, via-in-pad ground return (P6 layout item, not a sourcing concern).

LMG1020 VDD bypass, second (straddles the ball). DIELECTRIC SUBSTITUTED C0G->X7R: architecture (blocks.md/sheets.md) calls for '10nF 0201 C0G' but this does not exist as an orderable part - checked LCSC broadly, every 0201 C0G part tops out around 50pF (0 stock even there); 10nF at 0201 size is only physically achievable in X7R. This is not a P3 substitution of convenience: TI's own reference design (research/refdesign-classE-stage.json) specifies 'X7R or better' for this exact bypass network, so X7R is arguably the more correct call, and the architecture's own project-wide rule is 'no X7R in the TANK', not on the driver's local bypass loop. Flagging for P2/P4 awareness rather than silently deciding it - see OPEN.

Gate resistors, 2x per leg x4 legs. VALUE SUBSTITUTED 4.0R->3.9R: 4.0 ohm is not an E24 value and no such SKU is stocked; 3.9 ohm is the nearest standard value and clears TI's >=2 ohm floor with margin. 1% tolerance helps the +/-0.1nH gate-loop matching discipline (blocks.md s3) more than a 5% part would.

parts.role: L201 RF drain choke, PRE-AUTHORISED ESCAPE ROUTE (2x0.47uH in series - architecture's own documented fallback, not a P3 improvisation). No single LCSC part combines L>=0.82uH + SRF>=80MHz + DCR<=25mohm + Isat>=12A: every catalog power/shielded/molded inductor searched either omits SRF entirely (the norm for this part class - confirmed by checking research/raw/*.json and fresh searches across SRP/SPM/SDCM/wirewound/molded families) or the rare parts that DO publish SRF (Sagami/FH 'RF'/'high-frequency' 0603 chip inductors) top out at 300mA current rating, 40x short of the ~6-9A this choke carries. Series pair: combined L=0.94uH (14% over floor), combined DCR=8.2mohm (67% UNDER the 25mohm budget - dissipation will beat the 0.88W design number), each leg Isat 20A (>>12A required). SRF not datasheet-published for either candidate - this is not a new gap: the architecture's own research (refdesign-classE-stage.json) already states SRF must be verified empirically at bring-up (dummy load + RF detector sweep) regardless of any datasheet claim, because winding self-capacitance and nearby copper pull the real SRF down from nominal. Physically separate the two inductors per the escape route's own requirement (P6 layout item).

Bus HF decoupling bank, 4x of the 4x10nF+2x1nF pair. DIELECTRIC SUBSTITUTED C0G->X7R: architecture (blocks.md B6) specifies '100V C0G'; live search found genuine 100V/10nF C0G stock is effectively zero across every package (0805/1206 all 0 stock; the sole 1210 hit, C2310521, has only 96pcs - short of the 5x20=100 rule). This is a legitimate substitution, not a compromise: these caps sit on the +40V bus feed to L201, NOT in the resonant tank, and the assignment brief itself states 'X7R is fine on the DC bus but NEVER in the tank' - the tank caps (C_s/C_m, entry above) correctly stayed C0G.
Bus HF bank, terminates the bank's self-resonance. Genuine C0G in stock at the correct value/voltage/package - no substitution needed here.
